name: Crewlings
summary: A self-hosted AI agent. One Node.js process serves a private chat page, runs the agent loop against the Claude API, executes the tools Claude asks for on your machine, and keeps everything it knows in plain files. The agent loop and shared tools live in a core that a hosted edition will reuse.

runtime.language: TypeScript, run directly by Node (no build step)

components.does: Sends the conversation to Claude, streams the reply, runs each tool Claude calls (asking for approval when needed), feeds results back, and repeats until Claude is done. Saves after every step. It is handed its storage and tools, so it works the same on files or a database.
Defines what a conversation, tool, job and run look like, and the storage interfaces each edition must provide.
Reads schedules (intervals, one-time, cron lines), works out the next run, and every 20 seconds hands due jobs to the agent loop.
Memory, skills, schedules and chat search, each built from whatever store the edition supplies.
Calls HTTP APIs and fills in stored keys by name, only for the host each key is tied to.
Builds the agent's standing instructions, including memory and the skill list. Each edition adds its own lines.
Defines tools and checks the input Claude sends them before anything runs.
Serves the chat page and a small JSON API. Handles sign-in, refuses cross-site requests, streams live events to the page, and wires the core to local storage and tools.
Keeps settings, chats, memory, skills and jobs as JSON files, behind the core's storage interfaces.
The shell and the file editor, confined to the workspace, plus the list of tools and the prompt for a local run.
Drives a real Chromium browser through Playwright, if it is installed.
Empty for now. Built from stage 1 of the platform plan, on the same core.
The whole page, without a framework: chats, approval prompts, Memory, Skills, Schedules and Settings.
Turns the agent's replies into formatted text by building page elements directly, so nothing it writes can run as HTML.

flow.what: You send a message. The page posts it to the server and listens on a live event stream for that chat.
The server hands the message to the agent loop and returns at once. The run continues even if you close the page.
The loop sends the whole conversation, the system prompt (with memory and skills) and the tool list to Claude, and streams the reply to the page as it arrives.
Claude answers, or asks for tools. Web search, web fetch and connectors run on Anthropic's side and come back inside the reply.
For each tool Claude calls, the input is checked. If the tool changes something and approvals are on, the page shows a prompt and the loop waits for your answer.
The tool runs: a shell command, a file edit, an API call, a memory entry. Its output goes back to Claude as a tool result.
Steps 3 to 6 repeat until Claude replies without calling a tool. The conversation is saved to disk after every reply and every tool result.

tools.name: bash
tools.label: Shell
tools.does: Runs a command in the workspace folder, with a 2-minute limit.

tools.name: str_replace_based_edit_tool
tools.label: Files
tools.does: Views, creates and edits files, confined to the workspace folder.

tools.name: http_request
tools.label: API call
tools.approval: for anything but GET and HEAD
tools.does: Calls an HTTP API. Stored keys are filled in by name, only for their own host.

tools.name: browser
tools.label: Browser
tools.does: Opens pages, clicks, types and takes screenshots in a real browser.

tools.name: memory
tools.label: Memory
tools.does: Adds or removes long-term facts shown to the agent in every chat.

tools.name: conversation_search
tools.label: Search chats
tools.does: Searches the text of past chats.

tools.name: skill
tools.label: Skill
tools.does: Saves and reads procedures the agent wrote for itself.

tools.name: schedule
tools.label: Schedule
tools.does: Creates, lists and deletes jobs the agent runs later on its own.

tools.name: mcp_toolset
tools.label: Connectors
tools.does: Tools from remote MCP servers you add in Settings.

api.does: Sign in with the password (only when one is set).
Settings the page may see. Never keys or tokens.
Change name, model, effort, approvals, API key, stored keys, connectors.
List chats; start a new one.
Send a message and start a run.
Answer an approval: allow, always, or deny.
Live event stream: a full snapshot first, then each change.
List, add, pause or resume, and remove scheduled jobs.

data.holds: Settings, the API key, stored keys, connectors. Readable only by your user account.
One file per chat: the exact messages exchanged with Claude, tools allowed for that chat, token counts.
Long-term memory entries (8,000 characters in total).
Scheduled jobs and when each runs next.
The agent's working folder: the only place its file tool can reach.

features: server-side fallback when a request is declined

safeguards.name: Approvals
safeguards.what: Shell commands, file changes, API writes and browser clicks wait for your yes unless you turn approvals off.

safeguards.name: Workspace wall
safeguards.what: File paths are resolved, symlinks included, and refused if they leave data/workspace/.

safeguards.name: Secrets
safeguards.what: Stored keys are tied to one host, filled in outside the model's view, and scrubbed from responses. The shell does not inherit the agent's own API key or password.

safeguards.name: Local only by default
safeguards.what: Listens on 127.0.0.1. Refuses to start on a network address without a password.

safeguards.name: No cross-site access
safeguards.what: Requests from other websites, to other host names, or without a JSON body are refused.

safeguards.name: Safe rendering
safeguards.what: Replies are rendered as text nodes, never as HTML, under a strict content security policy.

safeguards.name: Limits
safeguards.what: 80 model calls per run, 2 minutes per shell command, tool output clipped at 30,000 characters.

deployment.how: npm install, npm start, open http://localhost:8787
deployment.notes: Scheduled jobs run while the program is running.

deployment.how: docker compose up -d --build, with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CREWLINGS_PASSWORD in .env
deployment.notes: Reach it through an SSH tunnel, Tailscale or an HTTPS proxy. The container walls off the shell.

covers: agent loop against a stand-in API and in-memory storage
local edition: shell, file wall, file storage
